Article Title: The OGs reunite: SAD gets 'bada bhai' tag in Punjab, but BJP has bigger ambitions
Article Text:
BJP, Akalis have reunited for the 2027 Punjab elections, but will nostalgia be enough?

Sukhbir Badal invoked his late father as he announced reunion with the BJP.

Why SAD-BJP patched up

The hot and cold relationship of SAD and BJP.

NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws. The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and the Shiromani Akali Dal ( SAD ) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections , reviving a partnership that once governed the state for 15 years across three terms.The reunion, announced on the Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, brings together parties whose relationship was famously described by former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal as "nau-maas da rishta", the bond between the nail and the flesh.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first."Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said in a post on X, adding that the partnership, nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, had "stood the test of time".Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced the reunion alongside BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, called the Akali Dal the NDA's "oldest ally" and said PM Modi had described the development by saying the "NDA is now complete".Shah also said SAD would retain its senior-partner status, adding that the "big brother" would get the chief minister's post. "Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats.Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," the Union minister said at the joint press conference.The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised.The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring, including Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi in August and a shift in SAD's position on the Centre's delimitation proposal. It also brings together two parties whose electoral fortunes have declined sharply since their separation.However, Punjab is no longer the state in which the old alliance enjoyed its strongest run. AAP has emerged as the dominant force, Congress remains a significant contender, and the BJP and SAD have both undergone changes in their support bases and political strategies.The partnership actually predates the BJP. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, shared power with the Akalis in Punjab as far back as 1967 and 1969. The modern alliance, however, was forged in 1996, when SAD's Moga Declaration pivoted from purely Panthic politics to a broader pitch of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat."The partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. It also helped both parties build a political coalition in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab.The alliance won 93 of 117 assembly seats in 1997, with SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. After losing power to Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 and retained power in 2012, winning 67 and 68 seats respectively.But the emergence of AAP, coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, weakened the alliance. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.The final rupture came in September 2020, when SAD walked out of the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws. Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister on September 17, and the Akali Dal formally ended its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP nine days later.The laws were repealed in November 2021, but the political damage endured.The alliance's decline is evident from its electoral record. In 2007, SAD won 48 seats and the BJP 19, taking their combined tally to 67. They improved to 68 seats in 2012, with SAD winning 56 and the BJP 12. But the numbers fell sharply thereafter. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three. By the 2022 assembly elections, the two parties managed just five seats between them, with SAD winning three and the BJP two.In 2022, SAD secured 18.38% of the vote and the BJP 6.60%, while AAP swept the election with 92 seats and a 42.01% vote share.Their separate performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections provided another reason to reconsider the alliance. The BJP failed to win any of Punjab's 13 seats despite securing 18.56% of the vote. SAD won one seat, Bathinda, with 13.42%.Together, their vote shares added up to nearly 32%, compared with 26.30% for Congress and 26.02% for AAP.The numbers make a case for pooling their support bases, although the combined vote share does not automatically translate into transferable votes or assembly seats.For the BJP, the alliance offers access to SAD's traditional rural and Sikh support networks. For the Akali Dal, it brings back a national ally and an opportunity to rebuild its electoral machinery, which is the BJP's strong suit.Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as more than an electoral arrangement."This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.The old partners are back again, but the state the BJP and SAD are returning to is markedly different from the one they left behind in 2020.The 2027 assembly election will be the alliance's first major state-level electoral test without Parkash Singh Badal, the five-time CM who died in April 2023. A towering figure in the Akali Dal, he was also a key bridge between the SAD and the BJP. Though Sukhbir Badal was already leading the party before his father's death, he now has to rebuild the party's standing without his political stature and influence.Another factor the alliance must keep in mind is that the farm issue has not disappeared. The repeal of the three farm laws did not automatically undo the distrust they created. Farmers' demands, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price, remain unresolved, keeping the issue politically alive in an agrarian state like Punjab. The BJP-SAD alliance will have to reckon with that trust deficit, particularly in the rural Malwa belt, which is the largest and most populous region covering major farming districts like Bathinda, Mansa, Sangrur, Patiala, Ludhiana and Muktsar.This is why the choice of Gurpurab for the reunion announcement is rich in symbolism. PM Modi had announced the repeal of the farm laws on the occasion in November 2021. The two parties have now chosen the same religious occasion to announce their political reconciliation. Whether that symbolism can translate into renewed trust among farmers is a different question.Another thing that has changed is that the Akali Dal can no longer assume that it commands the entire Panthic vote. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, independent candidates Amritpal Singh and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won from Khadoor Sahib and Faridkot, respectively. Between them, they also led in 15 assembly segments.This makes the party's return to its traditional Panthic space more difficult. The SAD has tried to reconnect with its core constituency through issues of Sikh identity and historical memory. The controversy surrounding 'Satluj', a film based on activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's work documenting alleged extrajudicial killings in Punjab, offered one such opportunity. After the film was taken down from an OTT platform, Sukhbir Badal announced screenings across the state, saying young people should know about the events it depicts.Six years on its own have transformed the BJP from a junior partner that contested just 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats into a more assertive player. Under the old arrangement, the SAD contested 94 assembly seats and the BJP 23, largely in urban constituencies. For the Lok Sabha elections, the split was 10 seats for the Akalis and three for the BJP.Its vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha election rose to 18.56 per cent, up from 9.63 per cent in 2019. The BJP contested all 13 seats in 2024, compared with just three under the old seat-sharing arrangement in 2019. Though it won no seats, the saffron party's vote share was higher than the SAD's 13.42 per cent. In the 2022 assembly election, the BJP had polled 6.60 per cent and won two seats.The party has also strengthened its ranks through a steady stream of defections. In April 2026, AAP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha led six other MPs into the BJP which included Sandeep Pathak, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta and Swati Maliwal. Six of these seven were Rajya Sabha members from Punjab. The exits dealt a major blow to the AAP's parliamentary strength and brought into the BJP leaders who had been closely associated with the party's Punjab strategy. Chadha and Pathak, in particular, had played key roles in the AAP's political and electoral planning.The BJP has since moved to put these former AAP leaders to work against their old party. Chadha and Harbhajan Singh have been named to its Punjab manifesto committee, while Pathak, Mittal, Sahney and other former AAP MPs have been assigned roles in the party's chargesheet committee, which will prepare its case against the Bhagwant Mann government.Earlier, in March 2024, AAP's then Jalandhar MP Sushil Kumar Rinku and Jalandhar West MLA Sheetal Angural had also joined the BJP. In November 2026, three more AAP legislators, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, crossed over. The BJP has also inducted senior Akali leaders, including Surinder Singh Chauhan and Jaswinderpal Sohal, as well as AAP functionaries from Moga led by spokesperson Navdeep Singh Sangha.The BJP's recruitment drive has not been limited to the AAP and SAD. Its Punjab ranks also include former Congress leaders such as Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Singh Badal, Ravneet Singh Bittu and Preneet Kaur.That changes the terms of the reunion. The BJP returns with a larger vote share, a wider organisational footprint and experienced leaders. The SAD, meanwhile, needs the alliance to recover lost ground and reconnect with rural voters. Amit Shah has announced that the BJP is okay with the junior-partner label in the alliance. It is, however, unlikely that the BJP will settle for the old seat-sharing formula.The immediate target of the alliance is the AAP government, which swept to power in 2022 with 92 seats and 42.01 per cent of the vote. Its vote share fell to 26.02 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when it won three seats, but it remains a formidable player.The SAD-BJP reunion gives the opposition a potentially stronger combination of urban and rural networks. It could also help consolidate voters who want an alternative to the AAP government. The drug problem, in particular, is likely to be a central campaign issue.At his press conference, Amit Shah listed three priorities for a future NDA government: eliminating drugs, eliminating corruption and strengthening nationalist forces. He promised that Punjab would be "completely drug-free" by December 31, 2029. He also targeted Congress, recalling Rahul Gandhi's 2017 promise that drugs would be eliminated within one term and accusing the party of doing nothing when it was in power.The attack gives the alliance a ready-made campaign plank. But it also puts the BJP and SAD on the spot, as both parties have been part of Punjab's political establishment for decades. The voters, thus, will judge their record as well as their promises.There is another complication. The Congress remains a strong third front and could split the anti-incumbency vote. Rural Sikh voters who continue to view the BJP through the lens of the farm agitation may also be reluctant to back the reunited partners. The AAP could benefit if opposition votes remain divided.The BJP-SAD reunion also complicates the Congress's position. With an established opposition pole, the contest for voters dissatisfied with the AAP government will now intensify. Amit Shah's attack on the Congress over its record on drugs made it clear that the alliance intends to take on both the ruling party and its principal rival.The Congress can still draw on its independent support base, but it will have to navigate a more crowded opposition space, as well as its own internal factional differences.Six years after a split that left both allies on the margins, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have chosen pragmatism over past grievances to challenge AAP and Congress. The 2027 election, however, will not be a simple replay of the coalition's past victories. And tough seat-sharing talks are yet to be held.The OGs may be back together, but winning over a changed Punjab will require more than old chemistry.
Article Summary: BJP and SAD announce revival of alliance for 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first.

Article Title: ‘Sitting at the feet of the same BJP’: Bhagwant Mann attacks Sukhbir Badal over alliance
Article Text:
Bhagwant Mann attacks Sukhbir Badal over alliance

BJP and SAD revive alliance after six-year break

NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Tuesday criticised the newly announced alliance between Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the 2027 Assembly elections, accusing SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of aligning with the same party he had previously criticised over its handling of farmers' issues.In a video statement shared by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Mann alleged that the Badal family had initially supported the three farm laws introduced by the Centre in 2020 but changed its stand after the farmers' protest gained momentum and widespread support.Referring to the resignation of then Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Mann claimed the Akali Dal had realised that it would struggle to survive politically in Punjab if it continued to support the laws."The BJP and the Akali Dal have formed an alliance. I would like to remind you of what they say to each other, how these people try to make a fool of the public. They feel that people forget things after some time. At first, the entire Badal family kept speaking in favour of these 'black laws', saying, 'That's a very good law, a very good law. It is amazing; if it does amazing work, then with this, the agriculture of Punjab will become very prosperous.' When the farmers' movement reached its peak and started getting support from all over the world, they realised this would be a mistake and that it would be difficult to survive politically in Punjab," he said."So, Harsimrat resigned and started speaking against those laws, claiming, 'The BJP is anti-farmer, the BJP is anti-farmer, we have sacrificed, the BJP is anti-farmer.' But by then, people understood that they were still in talks with each other and were separating from each other just to put on a show for the public," he added.Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet in September 2020, before the Lok Sabha voted on the farm bills. Days after the Rajya Sabha cleared the final bill, Sukhbir Singh Badal announced the SAD's unanimous decision to withdraw from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).Mann also accused the BJP of neglecting Punjab's interests, citing the state's tableau at national events on Republic Day and Independence Day."The same BJP says that the tableau that comes out on January 26 or August 15 will not be Punjab's tableau in Delhi. We got this work done by fighting with them," he said.Targeting Sukhbir Badal over his earlier criticism of the BJP, Mann alleged that the SAD president had accused the party of interfering in Sikh religious institutions with the help of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)."The same BJP about which Sukhbir Badal used to say that Sikh organisations are being taken over by the BJP with the help of the RSS, that the BJP has captured the committee of Hazur Sahib in Maharashtra and the committee of Patna Sahib. Today, sitting at the feet of that same BJP, you are making a political alliance," he said.Appealing to people to support the AAP government, Mann said, "Aam Aadmi Party is your own party. There is a party living in your hearts. I will come at your call, wherever you call me. We will come and raise our voice in favour of Punjab."Mann's remarks came after BJP and SAD announced on Tuesday that they would contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections together, reviving their alliance after a six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats, with the SAD taking the lead in the arrangement."Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats. Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," Union Home Minister Amit Shah said at a joint press conference attended by BJP president Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal."Naturally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will play the role of the elder brother. The Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will contest together. Both parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, while the Akali Dal will be in the role of the elder brother," Shah added.The announcement, made on Gurpurab, marked the revival of ties between the two parties, which ended their partnership in 2020 after the SAD withdrew from the NDA over its opposition to the farm laws.Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 Assembly seats, while the SAD fielded candidates in the remaining constituencies. The two parties had jointly governed the state for 10 years before losing the 2017 Assembly elections, when the Congress returned to power under Captain Amarinder Singh.In the 2022 Assembly elections, the AAP swept to power, while the BJP and SAD, which contested separately, were pushed to the margins.Meanwhile, the Punjab BJP on Monday announced its 16-member state election committee for the 2027 Assembly polls, with state president Kewal Singh Dhillon heading the panel.
Article Summary: BJP and SAD revive alliance after six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats, with the SAD taking the lead in the arrangement. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann accused SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of aligning with the same party he had previously criticised over its handling of farmers' issues.

Article Title: Watch: In a jibe on Meta, Abhijeet Dipke praises PM Modi, then calls for Constitution Day rally
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a Constitution Day rally in Nagpur on November 26. He urged people to join the event under the slogans of "Save Democracy and Save Constitution".In a video posted on X, he also took a sarcastic dig at Meta, alleging that social media posts glorifying PM Modi receive greater visibility and engagement on its platforms.The video begins with Dipke making remarks about PM Modi, saying, "In front of Modi Ji's radiance, the sun's light also becomes dim. In front of Modi Ji's speech, the sky's speech also becomes dim."He further says, "If there is Modi Ji, then this is a country. If there is Modi Ji, then this is the world. If there is no Modi, then there is nothing."He then reveals the apparent target of his sarcasm, saying, "This was for Meta, now let's talk about work." The remarks appear to be a sarcastic reference to what Dipke alleges is Meta's portrayal of PM Modi through excessive praise.Moving on to the rally announcement, Dipke said the Cockroach Janta Party would organise the event in Nagpur at 4 pm on November 26, coinciding with Constitution Day.Calling on people to participate, he said, "All of you have to come there and together we have to stand up for our country's democracy and constitution."He concluded by reiterating his appeal, saying, "Please be there on 26th November, 4 pm. Thank you."He ends the video with the song "Modi hai toh mumkin hai" playing alongside a photograph of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a Constitution Day rally in Nagpur on November 26. He urged people to join the event under the slogans of "Save Democracy and Save Constitution" In a video posted on X, he also took a sarcastic dig at Meta, alleging that social media posts glorifying PM Modi receive greater visibility and engagement.

Article Title: SCO: Pakistan set to invite India for culture ministers' meeting
Article Text:
The only significant visit to Pakistan from India after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack was by MEA additional secretary Alok Dimri for a meeting of the SCO national coordinators in September

After participating in the SCO inaugural civilisational dialogue in New Delhi, Pakistan is now all set to deliver an invitation to India for a meeting of the culture ministers it will host under its presidency of the Eurasian bloc early next year. It will be interesting to see how India responds as no Indian minister has visited Pakistan since the Pahalgam terrorist attack.Significantly, Islamabad is also preparing to host the SCO heads of state council summit - where India is usually represented by PM Narendra Modi -next year in late August, after initially considering having it on August 14 – Pakistan's Independence Day. An August 14 summit is unlikely to have seen participation by India at any level.The only significant visit to Pakistan from India after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack was by MEA additional secretary Alok Dimri for a meeting of the SCO national coordinators in September – shortly after Pakistan assumed presidency – to firm up the calendar of events under Islamabad's stewardship.After what is officially called Meeting of Ministers of Culture (SCO-MMC), Pakistan will also host more high-profile meetings of the SCO defence and foreign ministers in the run up to the Islamabad summit in August.The meeting for cultural cooperation among SCO member-states in Pakistan is a relatively low-stakes event for India that keeps political commitments minimal, unlike the foreign and defence high-level gatherings which might raise the political temperature at home.The last minister to visit Pakistan was S Jaishankar for a meeting of the SCO foreign ministers' meeting in October 2024, well before Pahalgam.Amid criticism by the Opposition for hosting Pakistan minister Musadik Malik for the Modi-proposed civilisational dialogue last week, India reiterated there was no dilution of its position on the Indus Waters Treaty that was "put in abeyance" after the Pahalgam attack. India has stressed that SCO cooperation should not be mistaken for bilateral thaw.The visit by Malik passed off smoothly without any bilateral friction as he adhered to the protocol of addressing multilateral SCO themes, rather than raising sensitive bilateral issues.While the key question remains whether Modi will travel to Islamabad for the SCO summit, Indian officials say such a visit is highly improbable at this stage. Any bilateral thaw that might result in Modi's visit requires, as far as India is concerned, a fundamental shift in Pakistan's position on cross-border terrorism.India is seeking tangible progress on its security concerns and doesn't want to create any optics of normalisation when these concerns remain unaddressed.The possibility of a senior minister, most likely Jaishankar, representing India is not ruled out. It would allow India to sustain its active engagement with the SCO, while not being seen as softening its Pakistan policy. Officials point to the fact that there's already a precedent for that. In 2024, it was Jaishankar who attended the heads of summit in Kazakhstan, filling in for the PM.
Article Summary: Pakistan is set to deliver an invitation to India for a meeting of the culture ministers it will host under its presidency of the Eurasian bloc early next year. No Indian minister has visited Pakistan since the Pahalgam terrorist attack. Islamabad is also preparing to host the SCO heads of state council summit next year in late August.

Article Title: ‘Chor hai tera chacha’: When Priyanka Gandhi slapped a boy in school over Emergency taunts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The 1977 election defeat followed the Gandhi family into childhood, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi recalled, sharing memories of school taunts and tense days at home in a candid conversation with their mother Sonia Gandhi , released in a video on Tuesday.In the video titled ‘What Ma Left Out of Her Book’, the siblings looked back at the days after their grandmother Indira Gandhi and uncle Sanjay lost the election following the Emergency, when the family moved to a different house and, as Priyanka put it, “there was a lot of tension in the air”.The conversation turned to their first day back at school after the electoral defeat. Priyanka recalled a boy approaching her with a taunt about Sanjay, who had been jailed in connection with the ‘Kissa Kursi Ka’ case.“I remember a little boy coming and telling me, ‘Tera chacha jail mein hai; chor hai tera chacha’,” she said. “So I gave him a slap and he started crying. We went to the teacher and I got a scolding.”The siblings’ recollections offered a glimpse of how the political upheaval of the Emergency years spilled into the everyday lives of Indira Gandhi’s grandchildren.Rahul, meanwhile, remembered a different kind of isolation at school.He said that when he sat down on the first day after the election, no one took the seat next to him. He did not say anything, but recalled that classmates were not talking to him and were being “a bit mean”.Sonia Gandhi interjected as Rahul spoke about the remarks children had made about their grandmother. The family also recalled a birthday party that Priyanka had arranged in an attempt to mend things. She had invited 32 children, but 15 minutes after the scheduled time, nobody had arrived. Eventually, only one friend turned up — a friend Rahul said he still has.The conversation also brought out the contrasting personalities of the two siblings. Priyanka said she had been a prefect and was suited to the school system, while Rahul described himself as rebellious, always asking questions and disturbing things.“She wasn’t rebellious. She always followed the rules,” Rahul said of Priyanka. “And I was rebellious, always asking questions.”Priyanka joked that the same difference could be seen in Parliament today, saying she was suited to the system while Rahul was not.The memories come days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which recounts episodes from her family life and the Emergency period.The 1977 election was the only electoral defeat for Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi. It followed the Emergency, imposed from June 1975 to March 1977, during which civil liberties were curtailed and political opponents were jailed.Sanjay Gandhi was convicted in the ‘Kissa Kursi Ka’ case in February 1979, along with former information and broadcasting minister V C Shukla, over charges related to the destruction of prints of the satirical film. The conviction was later overturned on appeal.Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi returned to electoral victory in 1980. Sanjay died in an air crash in 1981, after which Rajiv Gandhi entered politics and won the Amethi seat. He held it until his assassination during the 1991 election campaign.
Article Summary: The 1977 election defeat followed the Gandhi family into childhood, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi recalled. They shared memories of school taunts and tense days at home in a candid conversation with their mother Sonia Gandhi. The 1977 election was the only electoral defeat for Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday said his party was willing to make adjustments and accommodations to secure an alliance with the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, as seat-sharing discussions between the two INDIA bloc partners continued for the second consecutive day in New Delhi.Akhilesh said senior leaders from both parties were engaged in negotiations aimed at ensuring electoral victory, but refrained from disclosing details of the proposed seat-sharing arrangement, saying several aspects were still under consideration."Regarding the ongoing discussions, our party's senior leaders, along with those entrusted by the party to handle these talks, are currently engaged in the process. What exactly is being discussed? How many seats are being agreed upon, and how many could the other party potentially win? These matters are under consideration, so it is difficult to say anything definitive right now. Alliances are formed with the sole objective of winning; the purpose of an alliance is victory," he said.Emphasising the need for a united effort against the BJP, Yadav said the SP was prepared to make compromises given the electoral challenge ahead."The Samajwadi Party is committed to making adjustments and accommodations because the battle ahead is significant. The goal is to win, and we must win, especially against a political 'machine' like the BJP, we have to prepare accordingly and make the right decisions," he added.Akhilesh also questioned the functioning of constitutional bodies and the Election Commission of India (ECI), alleging that concerns were being raised over the possible addition of votes and the maintenance of electronic voting machines (EVMs)."Constitutional bodies have a duty to act fairly, yet questions are being raised about this very body. It is now being suggested that the BJP is planning to add approximately 3 crore votes. Furthermore, regarding the warehouses where EVMs are stored, who are the engineers tasked by the ECI with maintaining these machines? We are told that the machines are being 'serviced,' but no one knows who these engineers actually are," he said.After Tuesday's meeting, SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said the discussions had covered individual constituencies and described the negotiations as positive."Look, we have discussed every seat individually, and the discussions have been very positive. However, 403 seats are a very large number, aren't they? So, the discussions have not yet been completed. But you can rest assured that we will finalise everything in the next two meetings," he said.Ahead of the meeting, Ram Gopal Yadav had confirmed that the SP proposed allocating 26 seats to the Congress, including two constituencies won by the party in the 2022 Assembly elections, four where it finished second and 20 where the SP secured between 60,000 and 70,000 votes, while the Congress received around 2,000 votes."We have proposed offering two seats that the Congress won in the 2022 Assembly elections. Additionally, there are four seats where the Congress finished in second place, and 20 other seats where the SP secured between 60,000 and 70,000 votes, while the Congress received only about 2,000 votes," he told reporters.The Congress had submitted a list of 130 priority constituencies to the SP leadership during the first round of discussions on Monday. SP leaders agreed to examine the list and continue negotiations.Both parties agreed to contest the Assembly elections together and indicated that the seat-sharing arrangement could be finalised within the next two to four days.Describing Monday's meeting as cordial, Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said the discussions lasted around 20 minutes, with both sides approaching the negotiations positively."We took just about 20 minutes to wrap up day one of the talks in which we discussed the number of seats (with SP). The SP panel members heard us and said they would get back after talking to their party chief Akhilesh Yadav ji," Gautam told PTI.He said both parties were committed to contesting together and would reach a mutually acceptable seat-sharing arrangement. Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee president Aradhana Misra-Mona also indicated that an agreement was likely within the next two to four days.Tuesday's meeting was held at the residence of senior Congress leader Pramod Tiwari. The Congress delegation included Gautam, Misra-Mona, working president Imran Masood and Congress Legislative Party leader Virendra Chaudhary.The SP delegation comprised Ram Gopal Yadav, state president Shyam Lal Pal, MP Rajiv Rai, Awadhesh Prasad and MP Iqra Hasan.Meanwhile, SP leader Azam Khan said no one could stop him from contesting an election, expressing confidence in the party's election symbol."Who can stop me from contesting an election? My bicycle will contest the election; the bicycle will win... Samajwadis' focus is very narrow. They see nothing beyond the bicycle. These people don't even think about cars, helicopters, or airplanes..." he said.BJP leader and former Union minister Sanjeev Balyan said his party would seek to counter the electoral perception created by the SP and Congress during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and return to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term."We are making efforts to ensure that the perception created during the 2024 elections does not succeed this time. We will take these issues (development and law and order) before the people. The BJP will form the government again," Balyan told PTI Videos during an interview in Muzaffarnagar.The former Muzaffarnagar MP also dismissed the Congress's electoral prospects in the state, saying the party did not have a significant support base in Uttar Pradesh.On the SP's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) outreach, Balyan questioned the changing definition of the acronym used by Akhilesh Yadav."Let Akhilesh Yadav first give a final definition of PDA, then we can respond. Sometimes one group is included in it, sometimes another. If there was any PDA during his government, it was limited to a particular section of the backward communities," he alleged.Balyan further claimed that the SP government had failed to ensure adequate representation for different backward communities and Dalits, despite the party's current emphasis on social justice and representation.Asked whether the SP-Congress alliance's strategy, including its outreach through panchayats, had contributed to the BJP's defeat in several western Uttar Pradesh constituencies in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Balyan said electoral outcomes could not be attributed to a single factor.The 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly is scheduled to go to polls in February-March next year. The BJP has been in power in the state since 2017, winning two consecutive Assembly elections.The SP and Congress contested the 2022 Assembly elections separately. However, the two parties joined hands as INDIA bloc partners for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and jointly won 43 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 parliamentary seats.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav says his party is willing to make adjustments and accommodations to secure an alliance with the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Yadav refrained from disclosing details of the proposed seat-sharing arrangement, saying several aspects were still under consideration.

Article Title: 'NDA is now complete': BJP welcomes back 'oldest ally' Akali Dal ahead of Punjab polls
Article Text:
BJP welcomes back 'oldest ally' Akali Dal ahead of Punjab polls

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal , one of the BJP 's oldest allies, on Tuesday rejoined the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections , six years after the two parties parted ways over the contentious farm laws.Union home minister Amit Shah announced that the BJP and the SAD would contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab together, with hinting that chief minister's post going to the "big brother" Akali Dal.Addressing a joint presser in New Delhi, Shah welcomed the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led party back into the NDA and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had described the development by saying that the "NDA is now complete".Shah described the Akali Dal as the BJP's "oldest ally" and said the relationship between the two parties went back to the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-LK Advani era."Our relationship with Akali Dal has always been strong, our ties go back to Vajpayee-Advani era," he said."From today onwards, the Akali Dal will work in politics as an officially recognised ally of the NDA. As the entire country is celebrating Guru Parv, it is a matter of great joy for all NDA alliance partners that the Akali Dal, one of the NDA's oldest allies, is returning to the NDA once again… Prime Minister also spoke to Sukhbir Ji and the President with great joy over the phone. He expressed the sentiment that the NDA is now complete," Shah said.The reunion comes six years after the SAD walked out of the NDA in 2020 over the three farm laws introduced by the Centre, which had triggered widespread protests by farmers.Notably, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced the repeal of the three farm laws on Gurpurab, November 19, 2021. The two parties have now reunited on the occasion of Gurpurab, which falls on November 24 this year.Shah said the alliance would announce several key points in its manifesto, but set out its priorities at the outset. "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free."BJP national president Nitin Nabin said seat-sharing arrangements would be discussed later. "We will discuss seat-sharing arrangements in detail later, but today, by coming together, we are clearly conveying the message that we have united to serve Punjab. In the coming days, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji, we will continue our commitment to Punjab's development, just as we have always prioritised development and good governance. We will take the benefits of development to the last person in society," he said.Nabin also called the occasion a significant one. "Today is a very sacred day, and on this occasion, such a significant decision is being taken in the interest of Punjab and the country. I come from the city of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, and on this occasion of Prakash Parv, I believe the light of development, justice, and good governance will spread across Punjab. I extend my heartfelt wishes to Sukhbir Badal and to all the members of his party and to all the people of Punjab. Your joining the NDA alliance will strengthen all of us. I also believe that this alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal and our party is a natural alliance, a natural partnership," he said.SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, who spoke at the meeting with Shah and Nabin on Tuesday, described the tie with the BJP as one that goes beyond electoral politics. "This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.Badal said the alliance had been formed for the larger good and credited it with contributing to peace in the state. "This is an alliance for the interest of Punjab, for the interest of the country and for the interest of the Sikh community. You must have seen how long this alliance lasted and how many governments were formed; Punjab is progressing. There has been peace in Punjab. There has been brotherhood in Punjab," he said.He also underlined the historical role of his party. "Shiromani Akali Dal is not a new party. It is the second oldest party in the history of India. The leadership of Shiromani Akali Dal and the workers made the biggest contribution to the independence of the country. Even after independence, be it the issue of the poor, be it the issue of Punjab, be it the issue of labourers, be it the issue of the nation, Shiromani Akali Dal struggled," he said.The two parties are among the longest-standing allies in Indian politics, and have historically been partners in Punjab. The Akali Dal walked out of the alliance in 2020 over the Union government's intention to introduce the three farm laws, which triggered widespread protests by farmers. The laws were later withdrawn, but the two parties contested the 2022 Assembly elections separately.Their electoral record shows how much the split, and the years around it, cost them. The SAD won 48 seats in 2007 and 56 in 2012, its strongest performance, while the BJP won 19 and 12 respectively. Together, the two parties secured 67 seats in 2007 and 68 in 2012.The numbers fell sharply in the elections that followed. In 2017, the SAD's tally dropped to 15 seats and the BJP's to three, while the Congress won 77 and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) 20. In 2022, the SAD won just three seats and the BJP two. The Congress fell to 18, while the AAP registered a victory with 92 seats.Measured against its earlier record, the SAD's 2022 tally was 45 seats lower than in 2007 and 53 lower than in 2012, a decline of 93.75 per cent and 94.64 per cent respectively. The BJP's strength fell by 17 seats, or 89.47 per cent, from its 2007 tally, and by 10 seats, or 83.33 per cent, from its 2012 tally.
Article Summary: BJP welcomes back 'oldest ally' Akali Dal ahead of Punjab polls in 2027. Union home minister Amit Shah announced that the BJP and the SAD would contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab together. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the development by saying that the "NDA is now complete"

NEW DELHI: AIMIM Bihar chief Akhtarul Iman on Monday defended his controversial remarks comparing the way brides are dressed and presented at wedding receptions to a "tawaif", saying his comments were rooted in Islamic teachings and intended only for Muslims who wish to follow the religion."Tawaifs have more shame than your bahus," Iman said at a gathering.Iman's remarks, made at a public gathering (jalsa), have drawn criticism from political leaders across party lines. He had objected to the practice of dressing brides in traditional finery (solah shringar) and seating them at receptions for relatives and friends to see, arguing that Muslim women should observe 'purdah'.Responding to the criticism, Iman said observing the veil was obligatory (farz) in Islam and that his remarks reflected the teachings of Islamic religious scholars."India has a long tradition of Sufi saints and respect for women. Wearing sindoor is a matter of religious faith, and similarly, Islam requires women to observe purdah and wear hijab. No one should disrespect a religious scholar’s cap or tear a woman’s hijab. My comments were intended only for Muslims who wish to follow Islamic teachings, particularly regarding modesty and interactions between men and women," he told news agency ANI.His remarks triggered sharp reactions from political leaders, with several questioning his views on women's autonomy and the portrayal of women at weddings. Samajwadi Party MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel said the money given to brides at weddings was a form of blessing and that the practice was not limited to any one religion."The money given at weddings is essentially a form of blessing for the daughter; this is a practice found across all religions... The comparison involving Jamila and Sita touches upon the issue of women’s autonomy. It is not as if there is any indecent exposure; if a woman’s face is uncovered and she is adorned, what is wrong with that?.. The regressive notion that a woman must always remain completely covered is something that should not exist. .. I believe people, including our Muslim brothers, should oppose such thinking," he said.Congress leader Mumtaz Patel also condemned Iman's remarks, saying they were derogatory towards women and did not reflect Islamic teachings."It is very, very disgusting to see the so-called representatives of the community, especially coming from a party like the AIMIM that is supposedly representing Muslims, talk so derogatorily about women. Nowhere does Islam demean women like that. The religion or the culture does not treat women this way. There is a whole narrative being spread where statements like these make Islam a very easy target for everyone to condemn. I condemn this statement, and being a Muslim woman, I think it is absolutely, absolutely wrong..." she said.Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said different religions had different traditions, but accused leaders like Iman of promoting hatred instead of focusing on issues such as education, healthcare and employment."Different religions have different traditions. These people always talk about hatred. We never hear anyone say, at the very least, that we should talk about educating society, education, health, employment, jobs, peace and brotherhood. Why don't these people talk about these things? They spread this venom in society and conspire to defame it," he said.BJP leader Danish Iqbal also criticised Iman, accusing religious conservatives of trying to impose restrictions on Muslim women's lives in the name of Sharia. He said the Constitution had enabled women to pursue careers across different fields."In this country, regressive maulanas (clerics) have made numerous attempts to impose restrictions on the lives of Muslim women in the name of Sharia. They have sought to enslave them—effectively trying to extinguish their very lives. However, the Constitution of India has empowered Muslim women to such an extent that they are now becoming pilots, doctors, and boxers, excelling across various fields. Despite the persistent efforts of these maulanas—who have consistently used the fear of Sharia to exert control—the Constitution of India has paved the way for Muslim women to reach the pinnacle of success," he said.
Article Summary: AIMIM Bihar chief Akhtarul Iman defended his controversial remarks comparing the way brides are dressed and presented at wedding receptions to a "tawaif" He said his comments were rooted in Islamic teachings and intended only for Muslims who wish to follow the religion. His remarks have drawn criticism from political leaders across party lines.

Article Title: From 'nau-mass da rishta' to bitter rivals and back: How BJP-SAD relations played out over the years
Article Text:
How BJP-SAD relations played out over the years

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have come a long way from describing their partnership as "nau-mass da rishta", a bond as inseparable as nail and skin, to parting ways over the farm laws in 2020.Six years later, the two former allies are back together, reviving a political relationship that has shaped Punjab's electoral landscape for decades.The two parties announced their alliance for the upcoming assembly elections on Tuesday, bringing an end to years of political estrangement.During a press conference, Union home minister Amit Shah said that the two parties would jointly contest all 117 seats, with the Akali Dal taking the lead in the alliance.Shah said extensive discussions had taken place over the past three months between BJP leader Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal on issues concerning Punjab."Over the past three months, extensive discussions have taken place between Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal regarding the challenges faced by Punjab’s farmers, concerns over the state’s economic development, and the employment issues confronting its youth," Shah said.He added that the discussions had resulted in the preparation of a roadmap that would guide the proposed NDA government in the state."These deliberations have culminated in a roadmap, which will serve as the guiding framework for the NDA government that we intend to form," he said.This comes six years after the SAD walked out of the NDA in September 2020 over the Centre's three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed.The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have governed Punjab together for 15 years across three five-year terms. However, their political association goes back even further, predating the formation of the BJP.The Bharatiya Jana Sangh, the BJP's predecessor, was part of the Akali-led government in 1967 and 1969, following the reorganisation of Punjab.The alliance in its present form took shape in 1996, when the SAD, through its Moga Declaration, sought to expand its appeal beyond its traditional Panthic constituency by embracing the idea of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat".Coming in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab, the partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. Akali Dal stalwart Parkash Singh Badal used to describe the SAD-BJP tie-up as "nau-mass da rishta" - like nail and skin.Under their longstanding seat-sharing arrangement, the SAD contested 94 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats, leaving 23 for the BJP. In Lok Sabha elections, the parties contested 10 and three seats, respectively. The alliance won 93 seats in the 1997 assembly elections, with the SAD winning 75 and the BJP 18.After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the alliance returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab's trend of voting out incumbent governments. However, the emergence of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), along with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, dealt a major blow to the alliance in 2017. The SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.Three years later, the farmers' agitation against the Centre's agricultural reform measures brought the differences between the two parties to a head. On September 17, 2020, Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister. Nine days later, the SAD ended its 24-year-old electoral alliance with the BJP.Sukhbir Badal attributed the deterioration in ties to the BJP's growing numerical strength in Parliament, accusing it of not taking its allies into confidence on major policy decisions.However, the repeal of the farm laws in November 2021 did not immediately lead to a rapprochement. In the years that followed, the Akalis accused the BJP of interfering in Sikh religious affairs, even as several senior SAD leaders crossed over to the saffron party.The BJP, meanwhile, sought to shed its image as the junior partner. Its leaders argued that the alliance had constrained the party's organisational expansion in rural Punjab.In the 2022 assembly elections, the SAD, which contested in alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), won just three seats, with its vote share falling from 25.24 per cent in 2017 to 18.38 per cent. The BJP, which tied up with Amarinder Singh's Punjab Lok Congress and Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa-led SAD (Sanyukt), won two seats. The AAP swept the polls, securing 92 seats.Efforts to revive the alliance ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections failed amid renewed farmers' protests. BJP's vote share in Punjab rose from 9.63 per cent to 18.56 per cent as it contested all 13 seats, while the SAD's share fell from 27.45 per cent to 13.42 per cent. BJP failed to win a single seat, while the SAD retained Bathinda. Their combined vote share of nearly 32 per cent, however, was higher than that of either the Congress or the AAP, strengthening the case for a revival of the alliance.On August 7 this year, speculation about a possible alliance began after Sukhbir Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Parliament House. PM Modi reached out to Badal's wife and SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal to enquire about the health of Sukhbir Badal after he was attacked at a gurudwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded in AugustHarsimrat Kaur Badal, whose resignation had set the separation in motion, publicly recalled the developmental benefits of the alliance. Her brother and senior SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia also backed a reunion.
Article Summary: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have governed Punjab together for 15 years across three five-year terms. The two parties announced their alliance for the upcoming assembly elections on Tuesday. This comes six years after the SAD walked out of the NDA in September 2020 over the Centre's three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed.

Article Title: 'Once you have power, you may find excuses to keep it': Sonia Gandhi on turning down PM post
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi recalls dilemma over PM's post

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has said she felt the "pull of power" while deciding on whether she should take up the prime ministership in 2004, as she thought that she owed it to party workers who had rallied across the country during the election campaign to accept the post.She said it was a lesson about power that "once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it".The observations came during a conversation with her son Rahul Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, a video of which was shared by them on social media platforms.In the video shared days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love', the three are seen reminiscing about moments of joy, laughter and pain they felt at various points in time.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared the video and said, "Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage."In the video, Sonia Gandhi talks in detail about the internal conflict she faced while deciding whether to take up the prime minister's post after the Congress-led UPA's victory in the 2004 Lok Sabha elections. She asserts that she did not want power.Talking about the time, Rahul Gandhi says there was a situation unfolding and "we were witnessing the situation from the inside"."On the one hand there was mum saying maybe, maybe not. On the other side there were seven people. There is one gentleman over there who is the best possible PM," he recalls, referring to Manmohan Singh ."The interesting thing is there is only one man who can be PM because of his qualities, capabilities, and there are six-seven dreamers who cannot be. Then my mother decides - 'No (not taking up premiership)'; there is actually joy in the room," he says.Sonia Gandhi says there was another factor playing in her mind that can be called "the pull of power"."You may interpret it like that. But in a way I felt that I owed it to the people, especially the workers who throughout the country had rallied around to vote for the Congress. Since I was leading the campaign, I felt something towards them," she says"How can I let them down and say, 'Bye, I am going'. So that was also part of my thinking. Maybe it was something I wanted to believe for my saying yes," she says, adding that she was analysing her decision in retrospect.She says the experience offered a lesson about power: once one has it, they may find excuses to keep it."I did feel the sense of betrayal that I was betraying all those workers who had rallied around, come sun, come rain, food, or no food, to vote for the Congress," she says.After deliberating, Sonia Gandhi declined to become prime minister following the 2004 poll win and chose Manmohan Singh for the post.Priyanka Gandhi notes that Sonia changed drastically after Rajiv Gandhi entered politics and especially after his assassination.Rahul expresses disgust over the harsh personal attacks, abuse, and hostility Sonia Gandhi faced in Indian politics despite her quiet efforts to assimilate into Indian culture.Sonia Gandhi also recalled an incident during an opposition tour in Bihar when Rajiv Gandhi travelled in an open jeep, and stones were thrown at him amid inadequate security under an opposition state government.Rahul Gandhi alleged that Rajiv Gandhi's security was deliberately withdrawn to create circumstances for his assassination.Sharing the video on X, Sonia Gandhi said, "I wrote Belonging from my memories. Rahul and Priyanka added theirs, and the stories took on a whole new life.""My children are my greatest joy, my strength, and the two people who test my patience like nobody else can," she said.'Belonging: A Journey of Love", officially launched at a packed event at ITC Maurya here last week, was attended by the who's who of the Congress and the INDIA opposition bloc, literary figures and a host of chief ministers, including Tamil Nadu's C Joseph Vijay.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi says she felt the "pull of power" while deciding whether to take up the prime ministership in 2004. She said it was a lesson about power that "once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it" The observations came during a conversation with her son Rahul Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.

NEW DELHI: Six years after parting ways, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections , setting the stage for a potentially three-cornered contest against the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Congress.The announcement, made on Gurpurab , comes with a symbolic connection to the events that led to the breakdown of the alliance.Union home minister Amit Shah opened the joint press conference by extending Gurpurab greetings and describing the gathering as an "NDA ki press vaarta". Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal and BJP president Nitin Nabin were also present at the press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi."From today onwards, the Akali Dal will work in politics as an officially recognised ally of the NDA. As the entire country is celebrating Guru Parv, it is a matter of great joy for all NDA alliance partners that the Akali Dal, one of the NDA’s oldest allies, is returning to the NDA once again… Prime Minister also spoke to Sukhbir Ji and the President with great joy over the phone. He expressed the sentiment that the NDA is now complete," Shah said.The return of the BJP-SAD combine could reshape the electoral contest in Punjab, where both parties have struggled to regain their earlier political strength. Their combined performance in the 2022 assembly elections was significantly weaker than their showing during their years in power.The BJP-SAD alliance has been revived six years after the two parties parted ways over the contentious farm laws, which had triggered widespread protests by farmers.In a symbolic coincidence, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced the repeal of the three farm laws on Gurpurab, November 19, 2021. The alliance has now been stitched together again on the occasion of Gurpurab.The SAD-BJP alliance enjoyed its strongest electoral run in 2007 and 2012, when the Akali Dal retained power in Punjab for two consecutive terms. However, its fortunes began to decline in 2017 and hit a low in 2022.The SAD's seat tally fell from 48 in 2007 to 3 in 2022, a decline of 45 seats or nearly 94%. The BJP, meanwhile, saw its tally drop from 19 seats in 2007 to just 2 in 2022, a decline of nearly 89%.The Congress also witnessed a sharp reversal in its electoral fortunes. After winning 77 seats and forming the government in 2017, it was reduced to 18 seats in the 2022 elections.The AAP, meanwhile, emerged as the dominant force in the state, winning 92 of the 117 assembly seats in 2022 and forming the government under Bhagwant Mann.The renewed alliance will seek to combine the BJP's support among Hindu voters with the SAD's traditional Panthic base among sections of the Sikh electorate. The BJP is also looking to expand its footprint in the state, while the Akali Dal will seek to regain ground after its electoral decline.
Article Summary: Six years after parting ways, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The announcement, made on Gurpurab, comes with a symbolic connection to the events that led to the breakdown of the alliance.

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has revisited her long-standing concerns over the withdrawal of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s security, alleging that it was "deliberately" done to facilitate his assassination.In a candid conversation with her children, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, about her book ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, she recalled the fears she had raised over his safety and the events that deepened her concerns.In a video shared on X, Sonia said she had written the book using her memories, while Rahul and Priyanka added their own recollections, giving the stories “a whole new life”. NEW DELHI: Observing children should not be treated as toys in the custody battle between parents, Supreme Court Monday said such cases should not be decided only on a legalistic basis but children's choice should be given due weightage while deciding the case.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh set aside orders passed by a family court and Madras HC for granting custody of two minor boys, aged 16 and 14 years, under Guardians and Wards Act. The court passed the order after having an interaction with the boys who expressed their preference to remain with their mother. The court granted visitation right to the father."The object and purpose of the Act is not merely physical custody of the minor, but due protection of the right of the ward's health, maintenance and education. When the court is confronted with conflicting demands made by the parents, it has not only to look at the issue on a legalistic basis. In such matters human factors are also relevant. It is often said that children are not mere chattels, nor are they toys for their parents," the bench said."In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the considered opinion that the children should not be separated from their mother with whom they have developed a strong natural bond over the years keeping into account the predominant criterion of paramount consideration of the welfare of the child," it said.
Article Summary: Children's choice should be given due weightage while deciding the case, said SC. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh set aside orders passed by a family court and Madras HC for granting custody of two minor boys, aged 16 and 14 years.

Article Title: Swiss PIO in SC: Can govt protect my special child?

NEW DELHI: In an unusual case involving a 20-year-old severely intellectually challenged Swiss national of Indian origin facing destitution after death of his mother, Supreme Court thought out of the box and asked Centre whether it could take steps to create a mechanism to protect family assets allegedly being attempted to be pilfered by many fake guardians in Chandigarh.The petition was filed by the boy's father Sushant Sharma, who is also a Swiss national and who was granted divorce from the boy's mother by a Swiss family court in Oct 2014. The Lenzburg court had granted joint custody of the boy, who lived with the mother at Chandigarh since 2012.Advocate Balbir Singh told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana between April 2023 and March 2024, the boy, who suffers from 97% intellectual disability and can't decide for himself nor eat by himself, lost his maternal uncle, grandfather and mother. "He has no siblings. His father is his only surviving parent and natural guardian," he said.Sushant Sharma has ischemic cardiomyopathy with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30%, five stents, and an implanted defibrillator against sudden cardiac death. His condition is deteriorating and his cardiologist has advised him against long flights and stress. He cannot relocate to India or attend the several fora in which his affairs are being litigated.He has written that he seeks a stable system for his son because he cannot be certain of outliving him, Singh told the court.As taking the boy to Switzerland would uproot him from a synchronised and established care, language, relationships and surroundings, the father said, "The boy needs a structure in Chandigarh that protects him without depending upon his father's presence."Because the father and son are Swiss nationals, the National Trust Rules, which requires a guardian to be Indian citizen thus excludes father, the petitioner said, adding that Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act overrides other laws and offered only limited guardianship to him.Referring to multiple persons seeking to become the guardian of the boy ostensibly with an eye on the estate, the petitioner said after a lot of efforts Punjab and Haryana HC has appointed former CJ of Uttarakhand HC, Justice Ritu Bahri, as interim guardian.Sharma requested SC to "appoint a multidisciplinary Guardianship Committee on a 'Living Tree' model, its members selected on independent professional assessment and Centre holding a role of nomination and oversight, while there is still time. Hence this petition."SG Tushar Mehta said given the peculiarities attached to the case, he would seek response from ministry of social justice and empowerment how best the interest of the boy could be maintained. SC said, "We are entertaining this petition only for the limited purpose of seeking direct intervention of govt. The proceedings before HC will continue and Justice Bahri will continue with her responsibility.""Justice Bahri is requested to take assistance of the Chandigarh administration and identify movable and immovable assets of the families of the child and ensure they are duly protected," it said and posted the matter for hearing on Jan 7.
Article Summary: The petition was filed by the boy's father Sushant Sharma, who is also a Swiss national. Sharma has ischemic cardiomyopathy with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30%, five stents, and an implanted defibrillator against sudden cardiac death. He cannot relocate to India or attend the several fora in which his affairs are being litigated.

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing the fastest double century in List A cricket during India A's clash against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Doha on Tuesday.The 15-year-old reached the 200-run mark in just 52 balls, eclipsing the previous record of 103 deliveries held by Chad Bowes, who achieved the feat for Canterbury against Otago in Christchurch in 2024.Sooryavanshi eventually departed for a sensational 204 off just 53 deliveries, having struck seven fours and a staggering 28 sixes. His tally of 28 sixes is the most by any batter in a single List A innings, surpassing D'Arcy Short's previous record of 23 for Western Australia against Queensland in Sydney in 2018. It is also the most sixes hit in a single innings across professional cricket.The teenage sensation rewrote several other records during his extraordinary knock. He brought up his half-century in just 16 balls before reaching his century in a mere 28 deliveries, setting a new record for the fastest List A hundred. The previous record belonged to Jake Fraser-McGurk, who had scored a 29-ball century for South Australia against Tasmania in Adelaide in 2023.Sooryavanshi also reached 150 in just 40 balls, breaking the previous List A record of 64 deliveries held by AB de Villiers, who achieved the feat against the West Indies in Johannesburg in 2015. The effort also bettered his own previous record of a 59-ball 150 for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh in Ranchi in 2025.Sooryavanshi's extraordinary innings came after he had failed to make an impact in India's first two matches. The youngster explained that he assessed the conditions before backing his natural attacking game."I didn't score in the first two games. After assessing the wicket, I thought there was not much for bowlers so I decided to back my game. Mindset was same as every game, wanted to bat long," Sooryavanshi told the host broadcaster.Earlier, UAE had posted 249/8 after being asked to bat first, with former India domestic batter Harpreet Singh Bhatia leading their recovery with an emotional career-best 130 off 144 balls. Having lost two early wickets, Harpreet steadied the innings with crucial partnerships to take UAE to a competitive total.Arshad Khan was the pick of the India A bowlers, claiming four wickets for 43 runs.In reply, India A made light work of the 250-run target, reaching 253/3 in just 14.2 overs to register a seven-wicket victory. Whether facing pace or spin, Sooryavanshi stood his ground and repeatedly sent the ball sailing over the boundary.The emphatic victory was particularly important for India A after their defeat to Pakistan in the previous game. Article Title: Who is responsible? IndiGo flight flies Chennai to Bengaluru twice; 174 passengers return to origin after pilot aborts landing over unstabilised approach, sparking online outrage over missed connectio
Article Text:
In photos: Anna International airport (Chennai) ; KIA (Bengaluru)





CHENNAI: Passengers on an IndiGo flight from Chennai to Bengaluru on Monday evening were in the air and on the ground for nearly three hours, making the same journey twice, after the pilot aborted a landing attempt and turned the aircraft around.The flight, which was scheduled to leave Chennai's domestic airport at 4.20pm, finally took off late at 5.06pm. By around 5.40pm it was over Bengaluru airspace but never landed. The pilot deemed the plane’s final approach to be “unstabilised” as it approached the runway and opted to go around rather than risk a landing.The aircraft, instead, returned and landed in Chennai at 6.10pm. It was diverted to another airport. Passengers who had expected to be in Bengaluru by then were taken aback to find themselves back to square one. Some passengers asked cabin crew for an explanation and were reportedly told the plane had returned for "administrative reasons" and would be on the go shortly.The same aircraft took off again at 7.30pm with all the 174 passengers onboard and landed safely at Bengaluru at 8.15pm, almost four hours after its original scheduled departure.The pilot aborted the landing and decided to go around the unstabilised approach, sources at the airport said. IndiGo did not reply to requests for comment.An unstabilised approach is when an aircraft is not at the correct speed, altitude or alignment at a prescribed point before landing. A go-around is a normal safety procedure, not an emergency. Pilots are usually required to abort by aviation safety procedures in such situations.Readers replyThe episode sparked fierce online reactions. Many readers criticized the airline for its treatment of the affected travelers. One asked about passengers with onward connections to catch, a worry for anyone who had booked tight transfers in Bengaluru.Others concentrated on accountability, with one commentor asking who is accountable for the unstabilised approach in the first place. Another scathing comment said the pilot was not fit to fly "even a paper plane".But safety experts would likely see the pilot’s choice differently: the correct and professional course of action in the face of an unsafe landing is to abort it, even if it’s inconvenient. The frustration for passengers seems to be less about the go-around itself and more about the vague explanation given on board.

The flight, which was scheduled to leave Chennai's domestic airport at 4.20pm, finally took off late at 5.06pm. The pilot deemed the plane’s final approach to be “unstabilised” as it approached the runway and opted to go around rather than risk a landing.

Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has deleted X from his phone. The reason came out after Sunday's win. Lendeborg said he was being "baited" too much.
