NEW DELHI: India's bowlers had to put in a long shift during the drawn first Test against New Zealand in Wellington. With the attack delivering close to 250 overs across the two innings, the team management decided to cancel a planned team activity in Christchurch.India captain Shubman Gill said the players deserved a break after such a demanding effort. He also promised that the bowlers would be taken out for dinner."Our bowlers have put in so many overs, we will definitely take them (out for a dinner). We had a team activity but after bowling so many overs it stands cancelled," Gill said.The Indian bowling attack had a busy Test match, with the bowlers delivering 121 overs in New Zealand's first innings and another 120 in the second.Jasprit Bumrah bowled 49 overs across the two innings and picked up five wickets. Akash Deep bowled 43 overs and took three wickets, while Anshul Kamboj delivered 45 overs and claimed three wickets.Prasidh Krishna bowled 45 overs and took three wickets. Washington Sundar also put in a long shift, bowling 55 overs and picking up one wicket.Gill said India had started the final day well but could not make the most of their opportunities."We were very good in first session, were looking to get into the tail. Got two half chances and maybe could have been different. Energy was good and everyone was enjoying," he said.Gill also urged the ICC to reconsider its ban on using saliva to shine the ball. He said the Kookaburra ball was becoming soft too quickly, making it difficult for bowlers to take wickets on pitches offering little help.New Zealand batted for 75 overs on the final day, scoring 120 runs for the loss of three wickets. They finished their second innings at 239 for five, and neither team could force a result."We are way past Covid times. There was a rule that you can't apply saliva to shine the ball. It's been 7-8 years now, I still don't understand why they are not allowing it," Gill said.The India captain said the ball had lost its hardness early in the match."Our first ball, I think after 25-30 overs, the ball became very soft. I think they also complained," he said."We saw this in England as well. In the first 3-4 matches, we gave a slightly different ball in the Oval,"Gill also raised concerns about the quality of the Kookaburra ball. He said a softer ball makes it harder for fielders to take catches behind the wicket, especially when the pitch does not offer much movement."I don't know if the quality of the balls has come down or what happened. But in such conditions, if there is no help from the wicket, and the ball also becomes soft, then it becomes very difficult for the bowlers to take wickets," he said."They don't carry the edges. So, the caught-behind dismissal becomes harder. If there is not so much movement in the pitch, then the LBW remains on hold."Gill felt allowing saliva would help teams maintain the ball's condition for a longer period, particularly on flat pitches."And on the saliva, yes, I do believe that teams should be allowed to use saliva. It was a rule that was made effective during COVID. I think we are long past that," he said."The condition of the ball, if you're not shining the ball or if you're not able to maintain the ball well, especially on wickets like these, it makes the job of the bowlers very difficult."He said India had faced a similar problem during their 2025 tour of England, where the ball became soft early in the innings."Ideally, we understand after 50 overs, the ball obviously will go soft. But if the ball is going soft after 25-30 overs or it's going out of shape and you're also not able to maintain the ball and use saliva, then it's a very difficult job for the bowlers," he said.

Captain Shubman Gill says bowlers deserved a break after such a demanding effort. Gill urges ICC to reconsider ban on using saliva to shine the ball.

NEW DELHI: Delhi captain Priyansh Arya produced a breathtaking batting display on Tuesday, smashing a sensational 181 off just 68 balls against Tamil Nadu in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy to rewrite the T20 record books. He became the highest-scoring Indian batter in T20 cricket history, surpassing KL Rahul 's previous record, while also equalling the world record for the most sixes in a single T20 innings.The left-handed opener smashed an astonishing 19 sixes and 7 fours to power Delhi to a mammoth 275/5 in their 20 overs at the Daly College Ground in Indore. His 181 is now the second-highest individual score in men's T20 cricket, behind South African Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who scored an unbeaten 188 off 79 balls for Titans against Knights in the CSA Pro20 Cup in October 2026.Arya's innings eclipsed Rahul's 152 not out, scored earlier this year for Delhi Capitals against Punjab Kings in IPL 2026, to become the highest individual T20 score by an Indian.Sent in to bat by Tamil Nadu, Delhi suffered an early setback when Yash Dhull departed for eight in the third over. However, Arya ensured that the early wicket did little to derail Delhi's innings as he took the attack to the opposition bowlers.He found some support from Nitish Rana, with the duo adding 118 runs for the second wicket. Rana contributed 18 off 17 deliveries, but Arya did most of the damage at the other end.The Delhi captain raced to his hundred in just 36 deliveries, hammering 12 sixes and four boundaries in the process. He continued his assault after reaching the milestone, going past Rahul's Indian record of 152 not out before eventually falling for a remarkable 181 off 68 balls.His 19 sixes took him level with Finn Allen's record, set in June 2025, while putting him past Chris Gayle and Estonia's Sahil Chauhan, who had smashed 18 sixes each. Arya now shares the record for the most sixes hit by a batter in a single T20 innings.Arya's extraordinary knock provided the foundation for Delhi's imposing total of 275/5 in 20 overs. The next-best contribution came from Anuj Rawat, who remained unbeaten on 29, underlining just how much of Delhi's scoring was driven by their captain.Rahul's previous Indian record had come in spectacular circumstances as well. However, the mammoth total was not enough to secure victory, with Punjab Kings chasing it down with seven balls to spare.Interestingly, Arya was on the opposite side of that contest and played a significant role in the successful chase, smashing 43 off just 17 balls. He added 126 for the opening wicket with Prabhsimran Singh, who top-scored with 76 off 26 deliveries, as Punjab completed a remarkable chase.On Tuesday, however, Arya ensured that his name would stand above Rahul's in the Indian T20 record books, producing an innings that also rewrote the global six-hitting record.

Article Title: India, Malaysia begin Harimau Shakti military drill with focus on counter-terror ops
Article Text:
Indian Army contingent in Malaysia for Exercise Hiramau Shakti. (Image credit: Indian Army)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia, with 120 personnel from each side taking part. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30.The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate, with particular emphasis on synergising responses during counter-terrorism missions. The two armies will work in jungle and semi-urban terrain, relying on joint planning, tactical coordination and emerging technologies to improve interoperability.The exercise will unfold in phases. In the first phase, troops will first undergo cross-training to familiarise themselves with each other's operating procedures, followed by joint tactical drills. These include setting up a Joint Command Post and Surveillance Centre, counter-terrorism operations, raids, cordon-and-search drills and combat engineering tasks. Special attention will go to Unmanned Aerial Systems for reconnaissance and surveillance, along with counter-drone capabilities to detect and neutralise hostile unmanned platforms. The exercise will end with a validation drill built around a simulated counter-terrorism scenario, combining ground operations, integrated surveillance and unmanned systems.The fifth edition was held last year at the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan from December 5 to 18 last year. The Indian contingent then largely comprised troops from the Dogra Regiment, while Malaysia was represented by the 25th Battalion of the Royal Malaysian Army.The exercise reflects a wider deepening of defence ties. India and Malaysia established diplomatic relations in 1957 and a Memorandum of Understanding on Defence Cooperation signed in 1993 gave military engagement an institutional framework. The Joint Defence Cooperation Committee reviews existing cooperation and identifies new areas. In August 2024, the two countries elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.The naval dimension has grown as well. The fourth edition of Samudra Laksamana was held at Lumut from September 9 to 12 this year, with INS Mysore exercising alongside the Royal Malaysian Navy's KD Lekir and KD Gagah Samudera.In October 2025 INS Sahyadri visited Kemaman, while the survey vessel INS Sandhayak made a port call at Klang in July 2025. The navies of both nations also take part in multilateral platforms such as MILAN and the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise.Defence manufacturing is emerging as another area of cooperation. India is looking to expand exports to Southeast Asia, while Malaysia seeks to modernise its forces and diversify its sources of procurement. Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Bharat Dynamics Limited and BEML showcased their products at LIMA 2025. The two countries are also co-chairing the SEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM) counter-terrorism working group for 2024-2027.
Article Summary: The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30. The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate.

Article Title: Draymond Green gets dragged into explosive NBA legacy debate after Suns legend's brutal social media response
Article Text:
Draymond Green. Image via: Eakin Howard/Getty Images

What started the Draymond Green and Eddie Johnson argument?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Green questions Johnson's role, Johnson answers with numbers

Draymond Green and Eddie Johnson spent Sunday trading jabs on X over Green's Hall of Fame case. The former Suns Sixth Man of the Year started it after Warriors coach Steve Kerr said Stephen Curry's absence limits Green's offense. Johnson then asked if basketball is only a job for Green when Curry plays. The four-time champion fired back at Johnson's career and his analyst work. Johnson answered with a long list of his own numbers. Golden State has lost five straight games without Curry, which gave the argument extra bite.Kerr lit the fuse Saturday. "When Steph goes out, it really limits Draymond's impact offensively," the coach said. Johnson then posted on X (@Jumpshot8):"Name me a potential Hall of Fame player that will have that statistical personal résumé going into the Hall. Then you have players like Mark Aguirre, Tom Chambers, Shawn Marion, and Kevin Johnson not get in?"Green (@Money23Green) brushed it off: "Hahaha you named a bunch of players not named Eddie. Making it me vs. them is not changing your life, Ed."Johnson replied about 30 minutes later."My life is good, Draymond. Thanks for checking. I named Aguirre, Chambers, Marion and KJ for a reason. Your defense and impact on winning are part of your case. So here's the individual basketball question."He added his point with a question."How do you weigh that against the individual résumés of those four guys who could actually carry a team if the star player they played with is injured?"The last lines carried the sting. "Check my resume, even I did that many times. I got more players for you if you want? Just doing my job bro as an analyst. Isn't that your main job now and basketball is only when Curry plays?"Green's next post went after Johnson's role. Coming off the bench was "a great ROLE," he wrote, and he noted Johnson retired as the top scorer never to make an All-Star team.Johnson had numbers ready. He was a key piece on four conference finals teams, averaged about 22 points in 28 minutes during his Sixth Man of the Year season, scored over 20,000 points counting the playoffs and played in 94% of his teams' games across 17 seasons. "You said 'role' like it was an insult. Of all people, I figured you'd know better."He also plugged his podcast, Edification with Eddie Johnson. Green seized on it. "He's promoting his podcast!" he wrote, and added, "I'm happy to carry your show, though."Green scored nine points in the first quarter against Boston hours later, a season high.
Article Summary: Draymond Green and Eddie Johnson trade jabs on X over Green's Hall of Fame case. Johnson started it after Warriors coach Steve Kerr said Stephen Curry's absence limits Green's offense. Johnson then asked if basketball is only a job for Green when Curry plays.
